mainTopic: Reading the ביכורים passage, who owns new growths from a tree in someone else's field, and how much land comes with buying three trees
overview: The amud opens by finishing the reason why someone bringing ביכורים from trees he may not fully own does not read the ביכורים passage: the Torah requires that one person both take and bring the fruit. רב אחא בריה דרב אויא asks why he can't just read the verses anyway. רב אשי answers that it would look like a lie, and רב משרשיא says people might come to exempt the fruit from תרומה and מעשר. Next the גמרא asks what counts as growth 'from the trunk' versus 'from the roots.' רבי יוחנן says growth that sees the sun is from the trunk, and growth hidden underground is from the roots. The tree owner must still cut low growths, so that sediment can't later make them look like extra trees that would give him land. רב נחמן's tradition that 'a palm has no trunk' is explained by רב זביד as the owner giving up on it, and by רב פפא as palms simply not sprouting from the trunk. Finally the גמרא asks how much land a buyer of three trees gets, and רבי יוחנן begins to answer: under them, between them, and some land outside them, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Reading requires one person to take and bring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its reasoning: the ביכורים passage is only read when one person both takes and brings the fruit, and that is missing here.
steps.simpleTranslation: The passage is only read when the taking and the bringing are done by one person, and that is not the case here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its explanation of why the passage of ביכורים is not read in this case. The required condition, that one person both take and bring the fruit, is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ולקחת ('you shall take') and אשר תביא ('that you bring') in the פסוק are read as one package. They must both describe the same person. Since that is not true here, the reading falls away, even though the fruit is still brought.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking: picking or taking the ביכורים fruit
Bringing: bringing the fruit to the בית המקדש
As one: done together by the same person
And that is not present here

phrases.english: until the taking and the bringing are as one;
phrases.notes: This finishes a line from the previous amud. It's built on the פסוק 'ולקחת... אשר תביא', 'you shall take... that you bring' (דברים 26:2).

phrases.english: and that is not present here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes a derivation begun before this section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No reading of the ביכורים passage unless the same person takes and brings the fruit.

steps.title: Why not read the verses anyway?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא asks רב אשי why the person can't just read the passage, since it is made of ordinary Torah verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב אויא said to רב אשי: Since these are just verses, let him read them!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא challenges the rule that he does not read. Reading פסוקים from the Torah is always allowed, so what harm is there?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge says that even if the reading is not required, it should not be forbidden. Saying Torah verses out loud is normally fine. So the גמרא needs a reason why reading here would actually be a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, after all: opens an argument from something obvious

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Avya, said to Rav Ashi:
after all, they are verses,
let him read them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practical result of step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that he brings the fruit but does not read
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading Torah verses is always allowed, so even if the reading is not required, it should not be forbidden.

steps.title: It looks like a lie
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that reading would look like a false statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because it looks like a falsehood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains that reading the passage here would look like lying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ביכורים passage is a statement before ה׳ about the land He gave. A person who may not own the land would be saying something that might not be true. So the problem is not reading verses in general, but making this specific claim falsely.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Because it looks like a falsehood.
phrases.notes: He would be thanking ה׳ for land that may not be his.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason why reading is harmful here
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reading Torah verses can never hurt
steps.terutzMaskana: Here the verses are a personal declaration, and saying it would look false.

steps.title: Worry about skipping תרומה and מעשר
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא gives another reason: if he reads, people may treat the fruit as full ביכורים and skip תרומה and מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא son of רב חייא said: Perhaps he will come to exempt them from תרומה and מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא gives a second, different answer to רב אחא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real ביכורים are exempt from תרומה and מעשר. If he read the passage, the fruit would look like complete ביכורים, and people might stop taking תרומה and מעשר from it. Not reading keeps the fruit's special, in-between status clear.

keyTerms.meaning: To remove them, to exempt them
The portion given to a כהן
Tithe, a tenth of the produce

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the fruit is free of ביכורים rules. He still brings it as ביכורים. The point is that he must also take תרומה and מעשר from it, and reading could make people forget that.

phrases.aramaic: רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִיָּיא אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya, son of Rav Ḥiyya, said:
perhaps he will come to remove them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the fruits he is bringing.

phrases.english: from תרומה and מעשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 2, different from רב אשי's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason why reading is harmful
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reading Torah verses can never hurt
steps.terutzMaskana: Reading would make the fruit look like full ביכורים and lead people to skip תרומה and מעשר.
steps.whatToRemember: He brings the fruit but does not read. רב אשי says reading would look like a lie. רב משרשיא says it could lead people to skip תרומה and מעשר.

steps.title: What counts as from the trunk or from the roots?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about trees that grew and asks how to tell growth 'from the trunk' apart from growth 'from the roots'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they grew, he may not cut them back, etc. What is the case of 'from the trunk', and what is the case of 'from the roots'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about two trees bought in someone else's field. It asks for a clear way to define the משנה's two terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says new shoots from the trunk belong to the tree owner and shoots from the roots belong to the land owner. But the trunk and roots meet, so where is the line? This step sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How is it pictured?

phrases.english: If they grew, he may not cut them back, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. The land owner may not trim the branches of the two trees someone else bought in his field.

phrases.english: What is the case of 'from the trunk',
and what is the case of 'from the roots'?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי מִן הַגֶּזַע, וְהֵיכִי דָּמֵי מִן הַשׇּׁרָשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A clear test for 'from the trunk' versus 'from the roots'

steps.title: Above ground is trunk, below ground is roots
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that whatever sees the sun counts as from the trunk, and whatever is hidden underground counts as from the roots.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Whatever sees the face of the sun is from the trunk, and whatever does not see the face of the sun is from the roots.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question with a simple test: is the growth above ground or below ground?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line between trunk and roots is the surface of the ground. A shoot coming out of a visible part belongs to the tree owner. A shoot coming out of a hidden, underground part belongs to the land owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Sees the face of the sun: is above ground and visible

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's test is that above ground means from the trunk and goes to the tree owner, while below ground means from the roots and goes to the land owner.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
anything that sees the face of the sun,
this is from the trunk,
and what does not see the face of the sun,
this is from the roots.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Visible above ground means trunk. Hidden underground means roots.

steps.title: Worry that sediment will make the tree owner claim the land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's rule: if every visible growth belongs to the tree owner, buried shoots could later look like separate trees and let him claim the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we should worry: maybe the ground will rise with sediment. Then the tree owner will say to the field owner, 'You sold me three trees, so I own land!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's rule from step 6, that whatever sees the sun belongs to the tree owner. It points to a danger that this rule creates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose a shoot grows from the trunk close to the ground. Later, mud or sand from water piles up and covers the bottom of the tree. Now the shoot looks like its own separate tree, and someone who owns three trees in a field also owns the land under them. So letting the tree owner keep these low shoots could lead to a false claim on the land.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us be concerned / let us worry
Sediment, mud or silt that water leaves behind

phrases.english: But let us be concerned that perhaps
the ground will rise up with sediment,
phrases.notes: Picture mud piling up around the bottom of the tree, so the shoots growing from the trunk look like separate trees.

phrases.english: and he will say to him:
phrases.notes: The tree owner is talking to the field owner.

phrases.english: You sold me three [trees],
and so I have land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's rule from step 6 by showing the danger it creates in practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that anything visible above ground belongs to the tree owner
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Low visible shoots could later be buried by sediment and look like separate trees. Then the tree owner could falsely claim three trees and land.

steps.title: The tree owner must cut the growth
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, and רבי יוחנן too, rule that the tree owner must cut down that growth so no false claim can arise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said: He must cut it. And רבי יוחנן also said: He must cut it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem from step 7. The tree owner has to cut that growth down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The growth that sees the sun still goes to the tree owner. He simply may not leave it growing there. Once it is cut, it can never later look like an extra tree, so the fear of a land claim goes away. The גמרא adds that רבי יוחנן himself agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too said (someone else agrees)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman said: He must cut it down.
And so too Rabbi Yochanan said: He must cut it down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry of step 7 by requiring the growth to be cut.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a practical requirement that removes the danger
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The tree owner could simply keep the visible growth on the tree.
steps.terutzMaskana: He must cut it down, so it can never later look like a separate tree.
steps.whatToRemember: Growth that sees the sun goes to the tree owner, but he must cut it so he can't later claim land.

steps.title: רב נחמן's tradition: a palm has no trunk
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reports a tradition that a דקל has no גזע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: We have a tradition that a palm tree has no trunk.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן states a short tradition. The next steps argue about what it means, so this line sets up that discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement is short and unclear. Does it mean the owner of a palm doesn't get what grows from the trunk? Or that palms simply don't sprout from the trunk? רב זביד and רב פפא will each explain it differently.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold / we have a tradition
Trunk, and the shoots that grow from it

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: We hold by tradition
a palm tree has no trunk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the trunk of a palm tree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A palm tree has no גזע.

steps.title: רב זביד explains: the palm owner gives up on trunk growths
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד reads רב נחמן as a rule about rights. The palm owner doesn't get trunk growths, because the tree is expected to be uprooted, so he stops thinking about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד wanted to say: the owner of the palm has no rights to the trunk growths. Since the tree stands to be dug up and uprooted, he takes his mind off them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד offers his reading of רב נחמן's tradition. It is a rule about who owns what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד's logic is about the buyer's mindset. The tree in someone else's field will eventually be uprooted, and the owner can't plant a new one in its place. So the owner doesn't expect to keep anything long-term and gives up on growths from the trunk.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say (an idea that will be challenged)
To be dug up and uprooted
He takes his mind off it, gives up on it

steps.confusionAlert: The word סָבַר here signals that רב זביד's idea is about to be challenged. It is not the final word.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid thought to say:
the owner of a palm tree has no [rights to the] trunk,
because since it stands to be dug up and uprooted,
he takes his mind off it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the meaning of רב נחמן's tradition from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The palm owner loses the trunk growths because the tree is expected to be uprooted, so he gives up on them.

steps.title: רב פפא challenges from the buyer of two trees
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא points out that two trees bought in someone else's field also stand to be uprooted, yet the משנה gives their owner the trunk growths.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא challenged it: But one who buys two trees also has trees that stand to be dug up and uprooted, and yet the משנה teaches that he does have the trunk growths!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רב זביד's reasoning from step 10 using the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד said that being 'ready to be uprooted' makes the owner give up on the trunk growths. But the two trees in the משנה are in that exact situation, and the משנה still gives their owner the trunk growths. So that reason can't be right.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa challenges it:
But one who buys two trees—
they stand to be dug up and uprooted,
and it teaches that he has [rights to the] trunk!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב זביד's reasoning in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב זביד's reason that being ready for uprooting makes the owner give up the trunk growths
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's two trees are also ready for uprooting, yet their owner keeps the trunk growths. So the reason doesn't hold.

steps.title: רב פפא: palms just don't sprout from the trunk
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains רב נחמן differently. A palm owner gets no trunk growths only because palms don't produce growths from the trunk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: the owner of a palm has no trunk growths because a palm doesn't put out growths from its trunk.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a new explanation of רב נחמן's tradition. It is a fact about palm trees, not a special legal rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the palm owner has the same rights as any tree owner. There is simply nothing to own, because palms don't sprout from the trunk. This fits the משנה about two trees.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
the owner of a palm tree has no [growths from the] trunk,
because it does not produce [growths from the] trunk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב זביד's explanation after the challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the tradition as a fact of nature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The palm owner loses trunk growths because he gives up on them (רב זביד).
steps.terutzMaskana: Palms don't sprout from the trunk, so there is nothing to own.

steps.title: The משנה is difficult for רב זביד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב זביד deals with the משנה that רב פפא raised.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב זביד, the משנה is a problem!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רב זביד's view can survive. It sets up an answer on his behalf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא already moved to a new explanation, but the גמרא wants to know how רב זביד himself would handle the משנה's two trees. The problem is the same one from step 11.

phrases.english: But according to Rav Zevid, the Mishnah is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב זביד's view and repeats the problem from step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives trunk growths to the owner of two trees, even though they stand to be uprooted.

steps.title: The משנה is about buying for five years
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד explains the משנה as a special case where the trees were bought for five years.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is talking about where he bought it for five years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב זביד. The משנה is about a special purchase for five years, so his rule doesn't apply there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is moved to a special case. Here the buyer bought the trees for five years and has the right to plant a new tree if one is cut down. So the tree is not just waiting to be uprooted, and he keeps the trunk growths. In an ordinary purchase, רב זביד's rule still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רב זביד: the trunk growths are lost because the owner expects the tree to be uprooted (the משנה is a five-year case). רב פפא: palms simply don't sprout from the trunk.

phrases.english: Where he bought it for five years.
phrases.notes: In this five-year deal he may plant a new tree if one is cut down. So the tree isn't just waiting to be uprooted, and רב זביד's reason doesn't apply.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem of step 13 by limiting the משנה to a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about any ordinary purchase of two trees.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a five-year purchase, so רב זביד's rule still applies to ordinary purchases.

steps.title: How much land comes with three trees?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that buying three trees includes buying land, then asks how much land is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if someone bought three trees, he acquired land. How much land?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה about three trees. Then it asks a simple question to set up the next step: exactly how much land does the buyer get?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two trees, the buyer gets no land. With three trees, the משנה says he gets קרקע, but it never says how much. The גמרא wants the exact size of that land.

phrases.english: If he bought three, he acquired land.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. "Three" means three trees in someone else's field.

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the two-trees discussion behind and opens the three-trees clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size of the land the buyer of three trees acquires.

steps.title: The land under, between, and outside the trees
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the buyer gets the land under the trees, the land between them, and he begins to explain the land outside them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: this buyer acquired the land under the trees and between them, and as for the land outside them...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question about how much land is included. He lists the areas: under the trees, between the trees, and then starts to talk about the area outside them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Buying three trees is treated as buying the field area they form, not just the spots where the trunks stand. So the space between them is his too. The sentence continues past this point with the exact amount of outside land.
steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. "And outside them" is the start of a new detail, and the גמרא gives the amount right after this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
This one has acquired
the land under them and between them,
and outside them

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲרֵי זֶה קָנָה תַּחְתֵּיהֶן וּבֵינֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how much land is acquired.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The land under the trees and between them, plus some land outside them (the amount follows).
